newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors probe president Kim's son.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors probe president Kim's son.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Friday obtained a search warrant as part of a probe into rumours of a 200 billion won ($226 million) payment to President Kim Young-sam's son, a prosecution official said on Friday.
"The purpose is to confirm rumours that Kim Hyun-chul accepted 200 billion won ($226 million)," the official told Reuters.
State radio reported that the president's second son had taken the money from an agent of Hanbo Steel Co, which collapsed in January in a loans scandal.
The official said the warrant was for a search of the home and offices of the agent, identified by state radio and other national broadcasters as a close associate of Kim Hyun-chul.
Allegations that the president's son accepted money surfaced in parliament last month.

Opposition legislator Lim Chae-jung said there were strong suspicions the president's son took more than 200 billion won as a rebate on the purchase of German-made equipment for a new mill being built by Hanbo Steel.

Kim Hyun-chul issued an apology on Monday for causing trouble and anxiety, but without admitting any wrongdoing. His father said on television last month he felt shamed his son's name had been linked to the Hanbo scandal.
